what: Exelixis develops cancer medicines. Cabozantinib, sold as Cabometyx, treats kidney, liver and thyroid cancer and provides almost all of its revenue, with newer compounds in late-stage trials.
customers: Oncologists and hospitals, with treatment paid for by insurers and health systems.
moat: An established medicine in kidney cancer with years of clinical data and prescriber familiarity, protected by patents and settled litigation into the next decade.
risks: Almost all revenue comes from one medicine
Patent expiry later this decade is the central question
Analyst targets imply the shares are already fully valued
Pipeline compounds must succeed to replace the revenue
opportunities: Gross margin of 96% and return on invested capital of 29%
Revenue grew about 7% last year and about 13% a year over three years
Cash of about $892 million against almost no debt funds the pipeline and buybacks
watch: Cabometyx sales and late-stage results for its next-generation compounds.
